_doc: Size + comment ratchet. New files must stay under maxNewFileLines. Listed files must not grow. Comment share per directory must not rise. Lower these numbers as the refactor lands; never raise one without a note in 'exceptions'.

exceptions.desktop/tests/MainWindow.menus.gui.cpp: 1638 -> 1747 for one case: the Stencil Script row as a flyout — its place under the Assistant, its four actions, typing through the menu's re-dispatch, and a run that edits the canvas with the menu still open. It belongs with the other context-menu cases, and a QtTest binary runs one QObject of slots, so it cannot move without splitting the binary.
exceptions.desktop/tests/MainWindow.menuKeys.gui.cp: 557 -> 619 for one case: the script flyout's keys — the two-step Right onto its editor, Tab indenting instead of walking the actions, and Ctrl+Enter running. Same binary rule as above.
exceptions.desktop/src/support: comment share was raised 21 -> 23 with no comment added: theme.cpp's 817-line QSS literal moved to resources/app.qss, so the directory lost that many non-comment lines from the denominator. Ratcheted back to 21 once the header bodies moved into .cpp TUs: the declarations left behind are comment-dense, the moved bodies are not, and both live in support/.
exceptions.desktop/src/llm: comment share was raised 20 -> 21 with no comment added: ChatPlanTarget.cpp, a 605-line low-comment file, moved to app/ where it belongs in the layer order, so llm/ lost those lines from the denominator. Back to 20 after the llm/ TU splits.
exceptions.desktop/tests: the MainWindow GUI e2e is one QtTest binary per feature area (MainWindow.<area>.gui.cpp). Each area is still far over 230 lines: a QtTest binary runs one QObject of slots, so an area cannot be split further without splitting the binary again. The chat is four binaries for that reason — chatCards, chatCompact, chatDock and chatPanel/chatTurns — since one chat binary was longer than the whole rest of the suite run in parallel. The budget numbers above are the ratchet — drive them down as cases merge.
exceptions.desktop/src/app/MainWindow.hpp: 885 -> 890 for the script window: one QAction and three slots (open, the refresh a script shares with the toolbar, and the entry a dropped .stc uses). moc runs on this header, so a MainWindow member has nowhere else to be declared; the dialog, the core seam and the runner all live outside it. Back to 889 once the session draft went: the window opens empty. 889 -> 894 for the script FLYOUT: the panel action, the panel and its editor, plus ensureScriptMenuPanel — the context menu hosts the panel the way it hosts the chat one, and a MainWindow member has nowhere else to be declared.
251 -> 257 for the tooltip clock: a tooltip shows and hides on every hover, and at the shared 1.5x-faster dust speed its arrival read as a flicker, so TOOLTIP_DUST_IN_MS / _OUT_MS / _FADE_MS / _HAND_OVER_MS run that clock 1.5x slower. They sit beside the family they derive from; splitting four constants into a header of their own would cost more.
exceptions.desktop/tests/MainWindow.toolbar.gui.cpp: 1569 -> 1603 for one case: the script button's place in DATA, its image gate and its chord. It belongs with the toolbar's other section-order cases, and a QtTest binary runs one QObject of slots, so it cannot move without splitting the binary.
exceptions.desktop/tests/MainWindow.chatDock.gui.cp: 864 -> 921 for one case: the compact popover refuses every title-bar drag — the press, the move past the start distance and the double-click all leave its geometry alone, and the same gesture moves it again once it leaves compact, which is the half that would strand the panel undraggable if the flag ever failed to clear.
exceptions.desktop/src/dialogs/SettingsDialog.cpp: 374 -> 378 for one new Visuals row: "Dim and blur behind windows" (support/ModalBackdrop, browser vs-modal-backdrop). A row here is a checkbox, its tooltip and its label — the file is one long builder of them, and the only way to fit this one inside 374 was to cut the tooltip text of the row above it, which is user-facing wording, not slack.
